# GuardDog hosted-runner admission

This draft initially proves **only the native sandbox prerequisite**, not a dependency scan. A successful prerequisite is not a clean package result. No existing WHOIS/capability exceptions have been imported.

- GuardDog 3.2.0 and nono-py 0.16.0 have a complete hash-required, binary-wheel-only CPython 3.12 Linux x86-64 lock. The scanner is installed into a fresh virtual environment; no source distributions or package lifecycle scripts run.
- The Ubuntu 24.04 hosted job has only `contents: read`, checkout does not persist credentials, and the probe gets an explicit clean environment. It first calls the native `nono_py.is_supported()` before importing GuardDog (whose initializer can refresh popularity data).
- The actual kernel sandbox must allow an authorized synthetic file operation while denying a forbidden read/write and connection to a proven-live loopback listener. Time, memory, files and process counts are bounded. Unsupported capability fails closed; no `--no-sandbox`, fallback, or waiver exists.
- Bootstrap necessarily contacts PyPI (`pypi.org`, wheel delivery `files.pythonhosted.org`) with scanner dependency names/versions. `pip --isolated --disable-pip-version-check --no-cache-dir` disables optional version requests and ambient pip config. GitHub provides runner/action/checkout infrastructure. No application source, npm metadata, secrets or findings are uploaded to a scanner service; public Actions logs are not private.
- The prerequisite reads no project dependency archive and makes no GuardDog metadata/WHOIS/popularity requests. Full exact-lock archive scanning and findings review remain pending. Native `guarddog npm verify` re-resolves `package.json` selectors and is not claimed as complete lock-v3 coverage.

Official sources verified 2026-10-26: [GuardDog 3.2.0](https://github.com/DataDog/guarddog/releases/tag/v3.2.0), [native sandbox](https://github.com/DataDog/guarddog/blob/v3.2.0/guarddog/sandbox.py), [npm project resolver](https://github.com/DataDog/guarddog/blob/v3.2.0/guarddog/scanners/npm_project_scanner.py). Review owner: repository maintainer. Revisit this admission-only status before merging; it is not the requested final malicious-dependency gate.

## In-progress exact-lock investigation

The draft now downloads each exact public-registry lock-v3 name/version archive (including development, transitive, optional/platform and alias entries), verifies its locked SHA512 **before** parsing/extracting, and launches a separate native `nono_py.sandboxed_exec` worker. This is the same pre-exec sandbox mechanism used by GuardDog's `extract_sandboxed`; native `safe_extract` and `Analyzer` run entirely within it. No child inherits Actions tokens or arbitrary environment. The worker rechecks SRI, refuses archive links/devices/path traversal/duplicates, bounds compressed/extracted sizes, counts and ratio, and verifies readable regular files before analysis. Each invocation has native timeout/CPU/file/process/fd limits plus a 3 GiB address-space cap; controller concurrency is two.

Only npm registry metadata and exact archive GET requests are made by the controlled downloader, without redirects, credentials, lifecycle scripts or selector resolution. Responses have size/read/deadline limits; bounded metadata memoization reduces repeat package requests. Every native active source/metadata rule must return the expected result with no errors. A failed/missing package cannot become a clean scan. Synthetic native positive, benign, changed-SRI and forbidden-symlink controls run before registry scans; a package `preinstall` sentinel must never execute.

**Coverage is explicitly unresolved, so this investigation job remains blocking even when active-rule analysis completes.** `.github/security/guarddog.json` distinguishes active rules from unavailable WHOIS, stale-popularity and range-resolving recursive metadata capabilities. These are not false-positive exceptions, contain no historical exemptions and have not been accepted as the final policy. Exact-lock scanning of all transitive archives is not claimed to reproduce the native historical new-dependency rule. Bundled popularity caches are copied unchanged; any native import-time refresh attempt occurs only inside the network-denying kernel sandbox and cannot leave it. No fake freshness timestamp is written and no stale popularity verdict is accepted.

Actual native risk-engine findings are logged with package/version/SRI, matched rule/capability/path and file hash, without code snippets, maintainer emails, raw metadata or worker stderr. Raw source capability indicators are counted separately: they are heuristic inputs, not independently classified malicious verdicts. No raw scanner artifact is uploaded. All real risk/metadata findings still require investigation; no package is currently exempted. This intermediate state must not be presented or merged as a completed malicious-dependency gate.
